The integer \( n \) must satisfy \( 0 \le n < 18 \) and \( n \equiv -11213141 \pmod{18} \). This is equivalent to finding the remainder of \(-11213141\) modulo 18.

First, find \( 11213141 \bmod 18 \).  
We can compute the remainder by dividing 11213141 by 18:
- \( 18 \times 600000 = 10800000 \), remainder \( 413141 \)
- \( 18 \times 20000 = 360000 \), remainder \( 53141 \)
- \( 18 \times 2000 = 36000 \), remainder \( 17141 \)
- \( 18 \times 900 = 16200 \), remainder \( 941 \)
- \( 18 \times 50 = 900 \), remainder \( 41 \)
- \( 18 \times 2 = 36 \), remainder \( 5 \)

So \( 11213141 = 18 \times 622952 + 5 \), meaning \( 11213141 \equiv 5 \pmod{18} \).

Then \( -11213141 \equiv -5 \pmod{18} \). To bring this into the range \( 0 \le n < 18 \), add 18:  
\( -5 + 18 = 13 \).

Thus \( n = 13 \).

Answer: 13
